alex: Quick question — we're seeing a weird combo of HttpClient lifetime + Polly retries breaking streaming reads. Anyone run into this? (.NET 7, IHttpClientFactory, SocketsHttpHandler). We use ResponseHeadersRead but sometimes get 'The response stream was aborted' on retry.

ting: Yep. Classic set of traps. Short summary: retries attempt to resend requests, but HttpRequestMessage / HttpContent and the response stream aren't replayable by default. Also be careful not to dispose the HttpResponseMessage before you finish reading the stream.

maria: TL;DR checklist: 1) Use IHttpClientFactory (singleton clients) 2) Send with HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead 3) Build the HttpRequestMessage inside the retry policy so it can be recreated on each attempt 4) Make request content replayable or disable retries for non-idempotent ops.

alex: Can you share a minimal pattern that works? Right now we call client.GetAsync and GetStreamAsync from inside a Polly policy registered via AddPolicyHandler.

samir: Minimal pattern that avoids reusing the request and keeps response alive while consuming the stream:
```csharp
// inside policy execution (execute async lambda)
using var req = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, url);
var resp = await client.SendAsync(req, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead, ct);
resp.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
using var stream = await resp.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync(ct);
await stream.CopyToAsync(destinationStream, 81920, ct);
// response disposed after stream is fully read
```
Note: do NOT use GetStreamAsync which hides the response message; you need control of disposal.

ting: Also important: if you put the HttpRequestMessage creation outside the policy and then retry, the message can't be sent twice (HttpContent can only be sent once unless buffered). Always create new request inside each ExecuteAsync call.

maria: If you have HttpContent that is a stream (upload), you either have to buffer it (MemoryStream/FileStream with Seek) so it can be replayed, or you must not retry. For small bodies, copying to MemoryStream is easiest. For large uploads use resumable chunked approach.

alex: Aha — we were constructing the HttpRequestMessage outside the Polly Execute and reusing it. That explains the intermittent failures.

samir: A couple more gotchas:
- If you use AddPolicyHandler on the client, the policy wraps SendAsync calls. Make sure any DelegatingHandler doesn't dispose the response prematurely.
- If using SocketsHttpHandler, check PooledConnectionLifetime and server keepalive behavior — server-closed sockets mid-stream will abort reads.

maria: Example of registering with IHttpClientFactory and Polly (simplified):
```csharp
services.AddHttpClient("proxy")
  .ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() => new SocketsHttpHandler { PooledConnectionLifetime = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10) })
  .AddPolicyHandler(HttpPolicyExtensions.HandleTransientHttpError().WaitAndRetryAsync(new[] { TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1), TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2) }));
```
Make sure the operation you retry is actually safe to retry.

ting: Also, when reading long-lived streams, using ResponseHeadersRead is key. Otherwise HttpClient buffers the whole response which defeats streaming. But ResponseHeadersRead means the response message must stick around until the stream is fully consumed.

samir: Small helper I've used: extension CloneForRetry that recreates HttpRequestMessage and buffers content when small. Also a ReplayableContent wrapper that uses temp files for big payloads.

alex: This is great — moving request creation inside the policy and switching to SendAsync(ResponseHeadersRead) fixed our repro locally. I'll push a PR with the change and add a note in the SDK README about replayable content and streaming semantics. Thanks! :heart:
